title: Certified Marketing Professional
overview: In today’s highly competitive environment and challenging economic conditions, mastering effective marketing techniques is crucial to creating demand for products and services. The Certified Marketing Professional course equips participants with a comprehensive understanding of essential marketing concepts, including marketing planning, audits, communications, and research. This course is ideal for those new to the marketing field or for professionals looking to refresh and enhance their marketing expertise.
audience: This course is designed for a diverse group of professionals in marketing, public relations, communications, sales, and operations. It is particularly valuable for marketing managers from businesses and organizations of all sizes, across various sectors.
methodology: In addition to covering traditional marketing concepts, the course uses case studies, templates, and practical tools like Excel sheets to help participants develop key marketing skills and seamlessly apply them in their roles.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Define the marketing framework within an organization
Conduct comprehensive marketing audits to analyze micro and macro environments
Utilize best practices, tools, and models for effective marketing and sales management
Develop strategies and programs to build and maintain a competitive market advantage
Plan and execute advanced marketing strategies that drive organizational success

items.text: Key differences between marketing and selling
Criteria for segmenting consumer (B2C) and business (B2B) markets
Steps for segmentation, targeting, and positioning
Steps to create a promotional campaign
Evaluating the success of promotional campaigns

outline.title: The Product Life Cycle (PLC): A Strategic Approach

items.text: Marketing strategies for each PLC stage
Aligning promotion mix with marketing objectives
Characteristics of the promotion mix elements
Push and pull strategies across the PLC
Collecting and analyzing secondary and primary data
